comments.body: This occurs because the semantics of xla all_to_all vary from the supposed operations used in jax's all_to_all - xla first splits along split_axis, broadcasts across cores, then concats into the concat_axis.  the abstract eval rule for all_to_all is a simple identity which isn't correct as it's written, since in the above case the `f32[8,1,512]` shape is correct for the given xla operation.  In the simple case of split_axis==concat_axis as in pswapaxes everything works fine - the general jax all_to_all case would need a final transpose op to perform as described in the general case.

issue.body:
On an 8-device machine, if I run a trivial pmap + all_to_all with concat_axis=1:
```
x = np.ones((8, 8, 64))
y = jax.pmap(lambda x: lax.all_to_all(x, axis_name='i', split_axis=0, concat_axis=1), axis_name='i')(x)
print(y.shape, onp.array(y).shape)  # --> returns (8, 8, 64) (8, 1, 512) !!!
```
whereas
```
x = np.ones((8, 8, 64))
y = jax.pmap(lambda x: lax.all_to_all(x, axis_name='i', split_axis=0, concat_axis=0), axis_name='i')(x)
print(y.shape, onp.array(y).shape)  # --> returns (8, 8, 64) (8, 8, 64)  no shape disagreement
```
even just trying to print the repr for the former case `y` yields the error `<repr(<jax.interpreters.pxla.ShardedDeviceArray at 0x7fe547474d08>) failed: RuntimeError: Invalid argument: Argument does not match host shape or layout of computation parameter 0: want f32[8,8,64]{2,1,0}, got f32[8,1,512]{2,0,1}>`
issue.title: pmap all_to_all shape error

timeline.body: This occurs because the semantics of xla all_to_all vary from the supposed operations used in jax's all_to_all - xla first splits along split_axis, broadcasts across cores, then concats into the concat_axis.  the abstract eval rule for all_to_all is a simple identity which isn't correct as it's written, since in the above case the `f32[8,1,512]` shape is correct for the given xla operation.  In the simple case of split_axis==concat_axis as in pswapaxes everything works fine - the general jax all_to_all case would need a final transpose op to perform as described in the general case.

issue.body:
Code:
```python
def f(a):
  a = jax.lax.pswapaxes(a, "i", 0)
  print(a.shape)

print("pmap:")
jax.pmap(f, "i")(onp.ones((8, 8)))
print("\nsoft_pmap:")
jax.soft_pmap(f, "i")(onp.ones((8, 8)))
```

Results:
```
pmap:
(8,)

soft_pmap:
(1,)
```

issue.body:
When working on multi-host configurations, the `all_to_all` parallel primitive does not work due to not being in the whitelist at `jax.interpreters.pxla.multi_host_supported_collectives`.

My early experiments with it suggests that I was able to use it (or specifically `pswapaxes`) as a parallel `concat`, with the caveat that the order of the returned results was a little odd. Order wasn't important to me so this wasn't a problem in my specific case. :)

issue.body:
The previous rules assumed that `split_axis == concat_axis` (i.e. that
the used collective is equivalent to `pswapaxes`). Since we expose this
as part of our API, we should probably make sure that we handle other
cases too.

Fixes #1332.
